tip: Standard phrase to ask for the time.
Polite way to ask a stranger for the time.
translation_en: Excuse me, what time is it?

tip: Standard format for telling the exact hour.
'Viertel nach' means 15 minutes past the hour.
translation_en: It is a quarter past eight.

tip: 'Viertel vor' means 15 minutes to the hour.
translation_en: It is a quarter to nine.

tip: 'halb' + the NEXT hour means 30 minutes past. (halb zehn = 9:30).

sentence: Es ist fünf nach halb elf.
tip: In informal German, 10:35 is 'five past half eleven'.
translation_en: It is five past half past ten.

sentence: Es ist fünf vor halb zwölf.
tip: In informal German, 11:25 is 'five to half twelve'.
translation_en: It is five to half past eleven.

tip: 'anfangen' is a separable verb. The prefix 'an' goes to the end of the sentence.

sentence: Der Kurs fängt um neun an.
tip: Use 'um' for specific clock times. Separable prefix at the end.

sentence: Ich fange mit der Arbeit an.
Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
tip: 'aufstehen' (to wake up / get up) is a separable verb.
translation_en: I get up at seven o'clock.

tip: Because the time phrase 'Am Morgen' is in position 1, the verb MUST stay in position 2, pushing 'ich' to position 3.
translation_en: In the morning, I drink coffee.

tip: Standard word order: Subject, Verb, Time, Object.
translation_en: I drink coffee in the morning.

tip: 'Vormittag' is the time before noon. Verb in position 2.
translation_en: In the morning (pre-noon), I check emails.

sentence: Am Mittag esse ich in der Kantine.
translation_en: At noon I eat in the cafeteria.

sentence: Am Nachmittag mache ich eine Pause.
translation_en: In the afternoon I take a break.

tip: Exception! We say 'Am Morgen', but 'In der Nacht' because Nacht is feminine.
'schlafen gehen' acts like a separable verb phrase here.
translation_en: I go to sleep at eleven.
When do you go to sleep?

sentence: Ich arbeite von Montag bis Freitag.
translation_en: I work from Monday to Friday.

sentence: Von acht bis fünf arbeite ich.
tip: Time block in position 1. The verb 'arbeite' stays in position 2.
translation_en: From eight to five I work.

tip: Formal command with a separable verb.
'Wen' means 'Who' in the accusative case (Whom are you calling?).
'anmachen' means to turn on. Separable prefix at the end.
Yes/No question with a separable verb.
translation_en: Are you turning on the light?

sentence: Bitte machen Sie das Handy aus.
translation_en: Please turn off the mobile phone.
We are getting off at the train station.

tip: 'einsteigen' means to get on or board.

sentence: Ich hole dich am Bahnhof ab.
tip: 'abholen' means to pick someone up. Separable prefix at the end.
translation_en: I will pick you up at the train station.
When are you picking me up?

tip: Time in position 1, Verb in position 2, Subject in 3, Prefix at the end.

translation_en: Are you putting on a jacket?

tip: 'Passt es' is used to ask if a time is convenient.

sentence: Nein, am Montag habe ich keine Zeit.
tip: 'Zeit' is feminine, so the negative is 'keine'.
translation_en: No, on Monday I have no time.

tip: Standard phrase to arrange a meeting.
'frei haben' means to have time off.
translation_en: I have time off on the weekend.
I take a shower in the morning.

tip: Standard phrase to ask someone's profession.
Formal way to ask what someone does for a living.
translation_en: What do you do for a living?
He is a taxi driver by profession.

tip: Use 'bei' to say which company you work for.

translation_en: I have a lot of work.

sentence: Der Manager hat heute ein Meeting.
translation_en: The manager has a meeting today.

tip: 'checken' is widely used in modern German.
Use 'mit' (with) plus dative case when talking on the phone with someone.
translation_en: I am talking on the phone with my mother.
I am writing a text message.

tip: Common way to ask for someone's contact info.

translation_en: We are eating in the cafeteria.

sentence: Das Kind geht in den Kindergarten.

translation_en: Women are supposedly better at multitasking.

tip: 'inoffiziell' means unofficial (used for casual time telling).
'bearbeiten' means to edit. It is NOT separable.

sentence: Das Fragewort steht auf Position eins.
translation_en: The question word is in position one.
